title: Initiative: Quality guardrails gating for Optimize (mandatory eval checks before apply)
creator: Aditya Rao
description:
Overview
We’ve seen (and have customer-reported) cases where Optimize-driven cost reductions (batching/caching changes, quantization profile swaps, routing tweaks) introduce user-visible quality regressions (format drift, tool/JSON failures, reasoning degradation, higher refusal rates, etc.). This initiative adds mandatory quality guardrails that gate any Optimize-driven config application behind evaluation checks and regression thresholds.

Goals
- Prevent user-visible quality regressions when applying cost optimizations.
- Standardize how prompt sets, eval suites, and thresholds are defined, stored, and audited.
- Make gating outcomes actionable: clear pass/fail reasons, rollback hooks, monitoring/alerts.
- Provide a safe rollout path: feature flags, canaries, gradual enforcement.

Non-goals
- Replacing eval-harness (we extend/standardize outputs and suite selection).
- Fully bespoke, services-led eval authoring per customer (BYO prompt sets supported; not a services engagement).

User problem / why now
- Support escalations + anecdotal regressions are eroding trust in “Apply Optimize” (especially for enterprise teams with strict QA expectations).
- As we push more aggressive optimizations (quantization variants, more dynamic batching/caching), risk increases.
- Enterprise prospects are explicitly asking for auditability: proof checks ran prior to changes + controlled overrides.

In-scope behavior (definition)
- “Gating” is enforced at the control-plane layer when an Optimize proposal is applied via Console or API.
- For each proposed change, we select one or more eval suites based on optimization type + workload tags (chat/tool-calling/structured output; latency SLO; prompt length distribution; model family).
- We run eval-harness in “gating mode” to produce structured metrics, deltas vs baseline, confidence, and prompt-set revision metadata.
- Policy engine determines Pass/Fail/Timeout/Indeterminate based on threshold schema (min sample sizes, CI rules, per-metric deltas).
- On Fail: block apply (hard-block) once enforcement is enabled; provide reason codes and recommended next actions.
- On Timeout/Runner down: safe-degrade behavior depends on tier and rollout stage (observe-only → soft-block with override → hard-block).
- Override path exists (restricted roles), requires justification, is fully audited, and is rate-limited.

Key success metrics (initial)
- Quality regressions post-Optimize-apply (as measured by customer quality signals + internal sentinel suites): reduce by 70%+ QoQ once hard-block is default-on.
- Override rate: <3% of applies after 4 weeks GA (target; monitor for false positives).
- False-positive rate (blocked but later deemed safe): <1% of applies in GA cohort.
- Median gating runtime: <= 12 minutes for standard suites; P95 <= 25 minutes (TBD by suite sizes/runner capacity).
- Audit coverage: 100% of OptimizeConfigChange events include gating summary fields (suite, prompt-set rev, thresholds version, decision, reason codes).

Milestones / phases (target plan)
Phase 0 — Discovery (2–3 weeks)
- Define metric taxonomy, normalization, and initial threshold methodology.
- Prompt set coverage plan: required scenarios by product surface.
- Agree enforcement point + safe-degrade semantics.

Phase 1 — Build (4–6 weeks)
- Threshold schema + versioning; policy engine integration.
- Eval runner integration + caching + retries/timeouts.
- Console + API wiring for gating states and result display.
- Telemetry + audit events + dashboards/alerts.

Phase 2 — Pilot (3–4 weeks)
- Observe-only → soft-block for internal canary + design partners.
- Iterate on suite selection and thresholds to reduce false positives/negatives.
- Operationalize triage playbook.

Phase 3 — GA (2–4 weeks)
- Default-on hard-block for Optimize config changes (staged by tenant tier).
- Controlled override path with auditing.
- Post-launch retro + threshold tuning loop.

Cross-team ownership / DRIs
- Product (Optimize): Aditya Rao (DRI) — requirements, UX expectations, rollout policy.
- Applied ML / Evals: Jonas Weber, Selene Huang, Sana Farid, Karthik Iyer — metrics, suites, thresholds/statistics.
- Control Plane / Policy Engine: Ethan Park, Benji Okafor, Jordan Lee — enforcement, schema, determinism, auditability.
- Runtime & Performance: Mateo Alvarez, Sofia Ivanova, Noah Patel — runtime constraints; perf suite alignment; safe batching/caching.
- SRE: Sean Gallagher, Rafael Mendes, Miles Thornton — rollout, monitoring, paging criteria, incident playbooks.
- Telemetry/Analytics: Logan Wright, Nadia Rahman — metrics pipelines, data quality, reporting.

Primary artifacts (live docs / specs)
- PRD: sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/optimize-quality-guardrails-gating-prd.json
- Apply flow UX spec: sources/confluence/product-docs/design-specs/optimize-apply-flow-gating-ux-spec.json
- Metric taxonomy + thresholds: sources/confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quality-guardrails/guardrails-metric-taxonomy-and-thresholds.json
- Prompt set coverage plan: sources/confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/prompt-sets-and-benchmarks/optimize-guardrails-prompt-set-coverage-plan.json
- Eval runner integration: sources/confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/optimize-gating-eval-runner-integration.json
- Triage playbook: sources/confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/guardrails-failures-triage-playbook.json
- ADRs: 
  - sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-optimize-gating-enforcement-point.json
  - sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-threshold-schema-and-versioning.json
- Runbook + dashboards:
  - sources/confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/optimize-guardrails-gating-runbook.json
  - sources/confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/optimize-guardrails-dashboards-and-alerts.json
- Audit event spec: sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/audit-logging/optimize-config-change-audit-events.json

Open questions (needs closure in Phase 0/1)
1) Baseline definition: do we compare against “current serving config” or “last known good (LKG)” pinned baseline per route/model?
2) Tier policy: are Dedicated/Private allowed a different safe-degrade path when runner is down (manual approval vs block)?
3) Minimum eval suite requirements per optimization type: quantization likely requires stricter mandatory suites than batching/caching.
4) Statistical rules: CI-based thresholds vs fixed deltas for early pilot; handling flaky graders.
5) Timeout semantics: what is the default user-facing messaging and what counts as “safe” to retry?
6) Data retention: artifact retention windows vs audit log minimal fields; customer export/SIEM requirements.

Risks / mitigations
- Runner capacity/backlog causes timeouts → isolate eval traffic, set concurrency limits, caching, alerting, and tiered degrade policy.
- Overly strict thresholds block safe savings → iterative tuning loop + override + pilot gating modes.
- Under-coverage prompt sets miss real regressions → coverage plan + gap analysis + required scenarios for tool-calling/structured outputs.
- Inconsistent model/version identifiers across envs → explicit identity mapping work (ENG-3927) and telemetry validation.
- Override misuse → RBAC restrictions, second-approver discussion, justification required, audit log visibility, rate limits.

Definition of done (initiative-level)
- Observe-only gating available for all Optimize apply flows (Console + API), with logged decisions.
- Soft-block + override mode available behind feature flag for pilot tenants.
- Hard-block can be enabled by tier with safe-degrade policy defined and runbooked.
- Threshold schema is versioned and pinned to model versions + prompt set revisions; gating decision is deterministic.
- Dashboards and alerts live; oncall ownership defined; post-launch retro scheduled.

Notes
- This initiative is explicitly a trust & enterprise readiness investment for Optimize. We should keep messaging crisp: guardrails prevent regressions; they do not guarantee absolute quality.
comments: 2025-01-10 — Aditya Rao: Created initiative after SUP escalation on quantization apply. Goal is to make guardrails mandatory, not best-effort. Starting with observe-only for internal routes to learn false-positive rates.

2025-01-14 — Jonas Weber: Proposed initial metric taxonomy: task success + structured output validity + refusal/toxicity checks. Strong preference for CI-based gating where possible; fixed deltas may be ok for pilot if suite sizes are small.

2025-01-16 — Ethan Park: Control plane enforcement seems best for auditability + consistency across Console/API. Need ADR to lock this down; runtime-only enforcement won’t cover config apply paths reliably.

2025-01-21 — Sean Gallagher: SRE concerns: eval runner backlog can become user-facing “apply blocked” spike. Please define degrade behavior per tier + explicit alert thresholds for backlog/latency before pilot.

2025-01-27 — Selene Huang: Quantization needs a stricter policy: some model families exhibit formatting drift + tool-call JSON breakage even when aggregate rubric looks stable. We should require a small set of ‘format sentinel’ prompts for any quantization transition.

2025-02-03 — Aditya Rao: Updated scope to include audit event schema + override path requirements (requested by enterprise prospects). Splitting work into PM-843 (journey/UX states) and PM-844 (policy decision: which optimizations require gating + rollout phasing).
